newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: N.Korea not expected at parliamentary meeting.
newsitem.headline: N.Korea not expected at parliamentary meeting.

text.p: North Korea is not expected to attend this week's meeting of global lawmakers in Seoul, South Korean parliamentary leaders said on Tuesday.

More than 600 parliamentary deputies will gather in Seoul on Thursday for five days to discuss world security and stability at the 97th Inter-Parliamentary Union (IPU), Ahmed Fathy Sorour, president of the council, told a news conference.
Pyongyang was invited by South Korea, but so far the communist state has not responded, said South Korean National Assembly speaker Kim Soo-han.
"We regret that our efforts have not produced a fruitful result," said Kim, adding that two invitations had been sent to Pyongyang -- one in December and a second last week.
Kim said that North Korea was still welcome to attend at any time. "But at this point we are not all that hopeful the North Koreans will come."

South Korea was among 86 countries and 10 world organisations represented in Pyongyang when North Korea was host to the IPU conference six years ago. Talks at that meeting focused on nuclear non-proliferation.

The Stalinist state has been suffering from acute food shortages following massive floods in 1995 and 1996. The United Nations on Monday launched an appeal for $126 million to stave off famine in the North.

"North Korea could use opportunities like the IPU to bring up issues of food aid. It's too bad they haven't responded to the invitation," said Kim. "It's difficult to speak for a third party that is not present."
Kim said North Korea's food crisis would be raised during the conference, because it was an issue directly linked to security on the peninsula.
IPU officials said a resolution covering the most important issues would be adopted at the end of the conference.
More than 100 women parliamentarians will also meet on Wednesday to discuss partnerships between men and women in politics and prevention of sexual exploitation of children.
Women's issues are traditionally discussed on the eve of the conference.
Seoul hosted the biannual meeting once before in 1983 when 75 countries and 14 organisations came. Pyongyang did not attend.
